Within three hours this archive read **Cassaniti Gaetano** in the Piedimonte 1848 birth Tavola and **Venera Cassaniti** in two acts. They were in the registers the whole time; Piedimonte and Mascali are simply **not name-indexed**. **The nil was true and carried no information.** [Row 171](/worklist/).

rows.what: The nils that cannot be checked by a reader — nine, after the checker was checked
rows.note: **`tools/check_nils.py` is written, wired into the build and reports 27.** Of 220 searched rows, 173 assert no nil and 20 assert a nil *and say what the instrument could have reached*. **Twenty-seven assert a nil and say nothing about reach.** They may every one be sound — the checker cannot judge that, and deliberately exits 0. **What each needs is one sentence**: which comune, which years, which record types the instrument actually covers. **The worst of them are the ones that sound most conclusive** — «Trove — Prostamo before 1954», «Find a Grave — Prostamo and Melluso across Australia», «TNA Discovery — every surname and town of this family», «Antenati — Archivio di Stato di Messina, whole province». Each is a sentence about a family that may turn out to be a sentence about a search engine, exactly as [«Cassaniti returns nothing»](/searched/) was. **Coverage fails in three places** and all three render the same empty page: at the **collection**, at the **query shape**, and at a **single field**. Only the third is ever evidence about a family, and only once the first two are excluded. **Work through the 27 in the order the checker prints them.** **CORRECTION, THE SAME DAY: THE NUMBER WAS 27 AND IT IS NINE.** 27 came straight out of a regex written an hour earlier and never tested against the rows it judges. **Three errors, all in the tool.** Its nil pattern matched **rows full of findings** — «not one» caught *«NOT ONE AT NUDGEE»* inside a Find a Grave row reporting **eleven burials with plot numbers**. Its reach pattern **missed plain English**: *«BT 26 and BT 27 cover UK PORTS ONLY»* and *«CIVIL REGISTRATION IN THE PROVINCE OF MESSINA BEGINS IN 1820»* are reachability sentences, and were flagged for not containing the word «coverage». And the note claiming it would «under-report rather than over-report» was **backwards** — it over-reported three to one. **Fixed by looking for a BOUNDARY** of place, date or record type instead of for a vocabulary. **Three rows have since been given the sentence they lacked**, two of them badly needed: the Piedimonte birth-index sweeps for Maria Nicotra now say outright that the instrument could only ever reach children registered *at Piedimonte*, and she was registered at **Mascali**. **Nine remain**, and the honest lesson is the one this archive keeps paying for — a tool that judges evidence is evidence, and an untested one is an untested claim.

rows.what: The 115 documented people are invisible on the Atlas — fixed
rows.note: **The map draws places from the EXPORT's people, and the archive's best-documented people are not in the export.** That is why **Zambrone** — a comune with a read register run and a recorded gap in its deaths, 1813–1821 — has no marker at all, and why twelve of thirteen coverage rows match instead of thirteen. **`documented-additions.tsv` now holds 115 people**, every one of them added from a register this archive opened: the whole **Ventrice** line at Zambrone, **Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano** at Piedimonte, **Rosario Nicotra and Venera Murabito** at Mascali, **Gaetano Cassaniti and Maria Currenti**. **None of them is on the map.** **Why it is not a one-liner.** An addition carries a place as prose inside `source` and `note`, not as a structured field — there is no `birthPlace` to join on. Giving them coordinates means either adding a place column to the additions file or parsing the comune out of the source string, and the second is the kind of guess this archive does not make. **The honest first step is the column.** **And it would answer a question the Atlas cannot currently answer at all**: where the documented spine actually stands, as against where the family tree happens to name a town. **DONE, 22 September.** `documented-additions.tsv` now carries a **`place` column**, and the Atlas has a fourth layer, **The documented** — **89 people across 6 comuni, 79 of them in no family tree.** **The column is NOT derived from `source`**, and that distinction is the whole job: the source names the comune of the **record**, and the two come apart exactly where it matters — **Rosario Nicotra is named in a Piedimonte act and was a Mascali man**, and the act says so in the same line. Parsing the source would have put him on the map in the wrong town. So the column is seeded from the source's leading comune only where that prefix is a known comune, **overridden by hand where a document says otherwise**, and **left blank for 25 rows where nothing states it** — blank means *not recorded*, never *nowhere*. **ZAMBRONE HAS A MARKER FOR THE FIRST TIME**: eight documented people, no exported person, and a comune whose register run this archive has read. **Four gazetteer coordinates added** (Mascali, Giarre, Riposto, Zambrone), each checked against the bare-name fallback — unlike the Soriano Calabro entry, none of these corrects a collision, and the note says so. **And `check_additions.py` now refuses an unknown place**, because a free-text spelling would stop matching the gazetteer and the marker would vanish with nothing failing — tested by breaking it.

rows.what: GIARRE — the sixth town, where Giovanni Nicotra was born
rows.note: **A sixth comune, and it arrives with a document rather than a hope.** Piedimonte's **Matrimoni allegati 1872, fascicolo 20**, holds the publication certificate for Giovanni Nicotra and Venera Cassaniti, and the 1872 form prints **«nato a ____» separately from «residente a ____»**: **«GIOVANNI NICOTRA — NATO A GIARRE — residente a MASCALI»**. **That is why nine Mascali birth Tavole were empty of his household.** **Listed whole: 808 volumes, all at Catania, 1820–1873**, banked in `data/giarre-arks.tsv`. It is the **largest comune in this archive** — 164 Nati, 147 Morti, 131 Matrimoni, 44 processetti — it **holds two copies of every year**, and unlike Mascali it has 1844. **What to do.** (1) **Sweep Nati 1838–1848** at the N section for a Nicotra of a Rosario; his two declared ages differ by six years, so the window is the bracket, not a year. **1841 is done and has no N section at all.** (2) Then **Matrimoni 1833–1845** for Rosario Nicotra × Venera Murabito, whose Tavola names all four of their parents — **generation seven**. (3) Giarre's **processetti run from 1841**, which would carry birth extracts. **Containers banked:** Nati 1839, 1840, 1841, 1842, 1843. **ELEVEN YEARS SWEPT, 1838–1848, AND HE IS IN NONE OF THEM.** The N section is **absent altogether** in 1838, 1840, 1841, 1842 and 1845; **written and left empty** in 1839, 1843 and 1844; and holds **one entry** in 1846, 1847 and 1848. **The only Nicotra household at Giarre in eleven years is a titled one** — *«Nicotra D.r D. ALFIO / Consoli D.na ANTONINA»*, who name a Salvatore in November 1846 and again in January 1848. **Rosario Nicotra is a bracciante.** Different household, different class. **AND THE SWEEP IS NOT FINISHED, FOR A REASON IN THE PAPER.** The 1848 index says in its own Osservazioni column: *«in fine dell'alfabeto riportata altra volta la lettera M»*. **Giarre's Tavole append extra letter-sections AFTER Z** for late-registered acts — 1848 appends F and M, 1841 appends F and B. **So reaching Z is not reaching the end of the index.** **Five tails checked and clean:** 1838, 1839, 1840, 1841, 1848. **Six still to read:** 1842–1847. **Next:** those six tails, then Matrimoni 1833–1845 for Rosario × Venera Murabito, whose Tavola names all four of their parents. **THE SIX REMAINING TAILS ARE READ AND THE SWEEP IS COMPLETE.** 1842 appends T, P, B, F; 1843 appends R, M, C, G, T; 1844 appends a single G; 1845 appends F and T; **and 1846 and 1847 append nothing at all**, ending at Z with a blank leaf. **Not one appended N.** All eleven years — 1838 to 1848 — are now verified in **both the main run and the tail**, and Rosario Nicotra's household is in none of them. **So Giovanni says he was born at Giarre and Giarre's registers do not hold him.** Three readings survive, none proved: **his ages are wrong again** (he is 31 in 1872 and 28 in 1875, already six years apart — the windows either side are 1833–37 and 1849–53); **he was registered at RIPOSTO**, which was part of Giarre and separated from it in this very period, so a man from the lower town could say «nato a Giarre» and be entered there — *a hypothesis from general history, not from a document, and testable by listing Riposto*; or **«Giarre» is loose for a frazione** (Macchia, Trepunti, Altarello, San Giovanni Montebello). **Next: list Riposto.** **RIPOSTO ATTEMPTED AND NOT TESTED.** The listing returned zero arks, no facets **and no «Nessun risultato trovato»** — and the control, the same query against **Mascali** (listed at 498 three hours earlier), came back identical: **520 bytes, «403 Forbidden»**. The session is throttled. **«Riposto returns nothing» would have been a fact about the rate limiter.** Retry when it clears. **RIPOSTO IS OPEN, AND IT IS THE RIGHT KIND OF PLACE.** The throttle cleared; re-run with an *arithmetically impossible* control beside it (**Catania = 25,476**, which cannot be zero). **421 volumes, facet total 421, complete in one page**, banked in `data/riposto-arks.tsv` — 1821–1860 and 1866–1893 with a **gap at 1861–65**. **Three years read at the N section:** 1841 runs M straight into P with **no N section** (*but its last leaf is torn, so not a finished negative*); 1842 the same; and **1847 holds two entries, both NICOTRA** — *Nicotra Giuseppe × Autieri Angela* and *Nicotra Salvadore × Barbagallo Maria*. **Neither father is a Rosario**, so Giovanni is not there — **but the households are the finding.** Giarre's only Nicotra in eleven years is a *Dottor Don*; **Riposto has two ordinary ones in a single year.** That is where a bracciante of the name lived. **Still to read: 1838–40, 1843–46, 1848 and outward, and the torn tail of 1841.** **SEVEN RIPOSTO YEARS READ, AND THE TOWN HAS THREE NICOTRA HOUSEHOLDS.** 1838 holds one entry (*Nicotra Maria*, father **Francesco**); 1840, 1841 and 1842 have **no N section at all**; 1846's N heading is **written and left empty**; 1847 holds **two** (*Giuseppe × Angela Autieri*, *Salvadore × Maria Barbagallo*); 1848 holds one more of Giuseppe's. **Giarre's only Nicotra in eleven years is a *Dottor Don*; Mascali's in nine is an Alfio; Riposto has three ordinary households in seven** — and still not Rosario's. **1839, 1843, 1844, 1845 and the torn 1841 tail remain**, blocked only by the container throttle (four 520-byte 403s across two attempts). **One route that may not need them:** Riposto's 1841 births exist in a **second volume**, *17517 suppl. 2*, which may carry the leaf the first has lost.

rows.what: The 25 documented people with no place recorded
rows.note: **89 of the 114 documented additions now carry a `place` and are drawn on the Atlas. Twenty-five do not**, because their source is an index or a registration rather than a comune act — the Antenati name index, Queensland death registrations, New York parish baptisms, FindMyPast. **Each needs a person who has read the record to say where the person belongs**, and a blank is the honest value until then. **It is not a parsing job.** The rows whose source begins with a comune were filled deterministically; these are the ones where the comune is mid-sentence or absent, and guessing from prose is what [row 176](/worklist/) was careful not to do. **Work through them against the act, not the string.**

rows.what: RIPOSTO and MASCALI marriage Tavole, swept for Rosario Nicotra × Venera Murabito
rows.note: Twelve Riposto years (1835–1846) and eight Mascali years read whole. **Rosario is in none of them.** What the sweep did find is **Riposto Matrimoni 1844 atto 39**: *Nicotra Salvadore*, **patria Giarre**, son of Alfio Nicotra and Rosa Pappalardo, marrying Maria Barbagallo of Riposto — the father of the two Riposto children the birth sweep had already turned up in 1845 and 1847. He is not Giovanni's father and the pages say so twice. He settles the argument behind the search: see [Riposto](/riposto/) and [Giarre](/giarre/).

rows.what: RE-READ the Mascali birth Tavole whole — the junction method is not safe at this comune
rows.note:
**Mascali Matrimoni 1847 writes its sections in the order C, N, M.** 1841 and 1835 put V before S. So at Mascali «the alphabet runs M straight into P» does **not** prove there is no N section — the N may sit somewhere else entirely, and the only safe reading is the whole Tavola end to end.

The eight Mascali **marriage** years on [the Nicotra line](/nicotra/) were all read that way and are sound. The nine Mascali **birth** years of 1839–1848 were read at the M–to–next‑letter junction, which was the method before this was known. **They are recorded here as provisional until each one has been read whole.** Nothing found is withdrawn — Alfio Nicotra and Carmela Sudieri are still there in 1840 and 1847 — but the *negatives* are weaker than they were written.

rows.what: GIARRE, the early years — Salvadore Nicotra's birth act and the marriage Tavole
rows.note:
Two sweeps, one queue. **Giarre Nati 1821–1826**: Salvadore Nicotra married at Riposto in 1844, so his own act sits about 1815–1824, and [1820](/giarre/) — the first year Sicily registered anything — already holds **two untitled Nicotra households**, one of them a Rosario a generation too early to be Giovanni's father. Salvadore's act would name Alfio Nicotra's age and trade and say whether Alfio, Simone and Rosario are brothers. **Giarre Matrimoni 1835–1846**: where Rosario × Venera Murabito would be if he married in the town his son was born in.

**Blocked by the rate limiter and nothing else.** Twenty-one ark→container lookups were attempted on 22 September and exactly one returned. The limiter is **cumulative**, not per-interval — a three-second pause buys about twenty-eight lookups, not immunity — and a fifteen-minute wait after a lock was not enough. The images themselves are never throttled. This is a queue of about twenty-five containers a session, not a wall.
